title: Cocktail 2 Refuses to Fizzle. Day Two Pours Bigger Than Day One, and Shahid Kapoor Has His Third-Biggest Opener Ever.
excerpt: Fourteen years after the original became a Friday-night ritual for an entire generation of NRIs, Homi Adajania's sequel is holding its line — and the weekend numbers say the love triangle still works.
body:
The first *Cocktail* was the film you played at 2am in a Jersey City apartment, the one whose songs every desi wedding DJ from London to Toronto still keeps in rotation. So when **Homi Adajania** announced a sequel fourteen years on, the question wasn't whether anyone remembered. It was whether the magic could survive being bottled twice.

<youtube>https://youtube.com/watch?v=XXxUqLHq1xg</youtube>

The weekend answer, so far, is a quiet, satisfied yes.

https://x.com/TheStatesmanLtd/status/2067950775847010698

**Cocktail 2** opened Friday, June 19, to ₹13.10 crore — and here is the number that matters most: that figure makes it the **third-highest opening day of Shahid Kapoor's entire career**, sitting behind only *Padmaavat* (₹24 crore) and *Kabir Singh* (₹20.21 crore). For an actor whose February release *O' Romeo* limped to ₹7.75 crore, this is not a comeback. It's a vindication. The sequel out-earned his last outing by nearly 69 percent, and quietly bettered the opening of films like *Udta Punjab* and *Haider* that critics still genuinely love.

> "#Cocktail2: WINNER. More than lives up to expectations. Solid performances, superb music, stunning visuals, and captivating writing — this film scores on all fronts." — Taran Adarsh, 4 stars

Then came Saturday, and this is where it gets interesting. By late evening on Day 2, live trackers had **Cocktail 2** sitting at roughly ₹19.25 crore gross for the day — actually *climbing* over its opening, with occupancy jumping from 18.7 percent to north of 23 percent as the evening shows filled. (Different trackers count net versus gross differently, so you'll see the day quoted anywhere from ₹6.44 crore net to ₹19 crore gross — but the direction is unmistakable: up, not down.) A Saturday that holds or grows over Friday is the single cleanest signal a film has caught real word of mouth rather than just front-loaded curiosity.

The worldwide gross has already crossed **₹31 crore**, with overseas adding a healthy $0.70 million on day one alone — and that overseas line is the whole point for us. The original *Cocktail* was a diaspora film in its bones: Saif, Deepika and Diana drifting through London flats and Cape Town beaches, NRIs who'd built lives abroad and were still figuring out who they loved. The sequel leans straight back into that energy.

This time the triangle belongs to **Shahid Kapoor**, **Kriti Sanon** and **Rashmika Mandanna**, with **Sanjay Dutt** anchoring the ensemble. The pre-release song drops told you exactly what register Adajania was aiming for — *'Mashooka'* sends Shahid romancing Kriti through the honeyed light of Sicily, all playful, goofy energy that tips into a frankly seductive dance break; *'Tujhko'*, sung by Arijit Singh over Shahid and Rashmika, plays the heartbreak card, hinting at college sweethearts pulled apart by circumstance. Pritam scored it. Of course he did. The first film's soundtrack was half its legacy, and the team clearly knows the music has to carry the same emotional freight all over again.

For Kriti Sanon, the number is its own milestone — *Cocktail 2* is shaping up as one of her strongest post-pandemic openers, ahead of *Crew* and closing in on *Tere Ishk Mein*. She has spent the last few years proving she can headline; this is the kind of glossy, music-forward romance that lets her simply be a movie star, and she takes it.

On release morning she posted a heartfelt goodbye to her character, Ally — the kind of note that turns a film launch into something personal for the fans who'll watch it abroad this weekend.

The advance booking for Sunday is already strong — over ₹8.5 crore tracked, more than 269,000 tickets across 1,800-odd theatres — which means the all-important opening weekend should land comfortably in the ₹40-crore-plus range domestically before Monday's drop test begins.

For the diaspora, the where-to-watch is simple for now: **Cocktail 2** is in cinemas worldwide, including wide US, UK, Canada and Gulf releases through the usual desi-circuit chains. The OTT window, if the original's trajectory is any guide, will land on a major streamer within roughly eight weeks — watch for a JioHotstar or Netflix announcement once the theatrical run cools.

But that's later. Right now, fourteen years after the first round, the bar is still open and the diaspora's favourite love triangle is pouring strong. Some cocktails, it turns out, only get better the second time you order them.
